proofUses.reason: The deterministic argument uses order of real flows and backward continuation to locate the collision tip. Local Schwarz reflection proves that preceding compact intervals are separated from the future domain; full inverse-map boundary continuity is an explicit hypothesis.

The deterministic collision equivalence and the proved co-swallowing law remove the geometric input retained in 2L0Z. The beta tail excludes a hit at each fixed real point and gives positive probability that a prescribed interval is separated from the domain. The trace theorem is supplied by MN2A.

At the finite swallowing time of one, all boundary preimages of zero form a compact set strictly left of the driver. A measurable deterministic interval contains that set with positive probability. Strong Markov and interval swallowing give eventual separation; scaling and the Brownian germ law give separation at every positive time.

The monotone distance from zero to the domain has square-root scaling and tends to infinity. Future tips stay outside each earlier domain distance. Every compact set is covered by a hull, and local real-flow continuation excludes any surviving real point inside the growing half-disk. No uncountable intersection of fixed-point events is used.
